issues.body: `GateState.from_dict` independently accepts every present persisted field and defaults missing fields. Consequently a partial carrier such as `{"attempt": max_total_polls - 1}` preserves an almost-exhausted budget while resetting `stable`, history, and the other coupled decision state. On the next one-shot evaluation, a single terminal-green observation advances `attempt` to the maximum; because the normal settle condition is not met, `run_gate_once` calls `render_budget_exhausted`, whose pending-zero graceful-timeout path renders that one observation green. This contradicts the stated fail-safe property that unreadable/partial state restarts the window and never shortens it. A truncated write that remains valid JSON, a schema-version mismatch, or manual/cache corruption can therefore manufacture a premature pass once this entry point is wired.
issues.fix_hint: Validate the persisted carrier as one atomic, versioned record before accepting any of it: require exactly all persisted fields with strict types/ranges and cross-field invariants, otherwise return a completely fresh `GateState` (including `attempt = 0`). Prefer atomic temp-file-plus-rename writes as well. Add a real-path test using an almost-exhausted partial JSON state and a terminal-green fetch, asserting it cannot return 0 after one observation; update the existing partial-state test to require a full restart rather than preserving `attempt`.
issues.title: Partial persisted state can bypass the settle and startup safety windows

verdict.summary: The resident-loop extraction appears structurally faithful, but the new persisted-state boundary can accept a partial yet syntactically valid state that shortens the safety windows and can produce a premature green verdict. The tests explicitly encode this unsafe behavior by retaining `attempt` while resetting omitted fields, despite the implementation and documentation claiming that partial/corrupt state only restarts the window. This must be fixed before the one-shot seam is considered correct, even though it is not wired to the required check yet.
